new_statements.quote: [p. 164] The stress systems are also very similar at the word level, with stress generally falling on the last syllable in nouns and adjectives but having a tendency towards the initial position in verbs. [p. 171] Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress. Thus, there is hardly any motivation to assume binary feet of any kind for this language […] In all of the verbs we examined, the stress is on the preverb; yet raising targets the preverb in some cases and the stem in others.
new_statements.citation: Mahdavi Mazdeh, Mohsen & Sarah Nehzati. 2024. Low vowel dissimilation in Mazandarani. Journal of Iranian Linguistics 1(1): 163-183. doi:10.46991/jil/2024.01.08
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opens (26-page PDF, text layer, no scanned needed); PDF p. 6 is the title page 'Low vowel dissimilation in Mazandarani', JIL 1 (2024): 163-183, doi.org/10.46991/jil/2024.01.08, CC BY-NC 4.0. Both quoted segments are present word for word at the stated locators (extracted text): PDF p. 7 = printed p. 164, §1 Introduction: 'The stress systems are also very similar at the word level, with stress generally falling on the last syllable in nouns and adjectives but having a tendency towards the initial position in verbs.' PDF p. 14 = printed p. 171, §2: 'Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress. Thus, there is hardly any motivation to assume bin…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type part-of-speech-conditioned word stress: in nouns and adjectives primary stress falls on the final syllable of the word; in verbs it tends to the initial syllable, specifically the preverb/prefix (ba-, da-, de-, ha-, hā-) in prefixed verb forms (confirmed independently by Mokhtarian 2005: 15, 'Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich'). No secondary stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly denied: 'Mazandarani (like most — perhaps all — Iranian languages) does not have secondary stress' (p. 171).
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: stress on the preverb/initial syllable rather than final (pp. 164, 171, 178). Mokhtarian 2005 (Tübingen dissertation, pp. 10-17) adds that plural -(h)ā/-un, definite-object -e, attributive -e and indirect-object -ra are unstressed (so stress stays on the stem-final syllable), while substantivizing -i and the infinitive ending -(j)en are stressed and preterite prefixes attract the word accent. The p. 164 statement is hedged with 'generally' and is a comparison with Persian, not an exhaustive rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('at the word level'); citation/elicited forms from native speakers of the Amol, Babol and Reineh dialects. The article's topic is vowel dissimilation, so the stress statement is brief background, not a dedicated prosodic analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Mahdavi Mazdeh & Nehzati 2024 describe the dialects of Amol, Babol and Reineh (Larijan, south of Amol) in central Mazandaran, all within Glottolog's single language maza1291; Mokhtarian 2005 sketches 'the present-day Mazandarani dialect' without naming a locality. The earlier scan's named sources (Yoshie 1996, Nawata 1984) concern the Sari dialect, also maza1291. Glottolog's other refs Borjian 2012 (Velātru/Gachsar) and 2013 (Yushij) describe Caspian-Persian transition-zone varieties in the Alborz, not the core language.

sources.note: p. 164: word stress generally on the last syllable in nouns and adjectives, tendency towards initial position in verbs; p. 171: no secondary stress, stress on the preverb in all verbs examined; p. 178: first syllable stressed in prefixed verbs (Reineh). Dialects of Amol, Babol, Reineh; data from elicitation with native speakers.

sources.citation: Mokhtarian, Bahar. 2005 [2004]. Die Maqāmen des Ḥarīrī in tabarischer Übersetzung (I-VII) nach einer Teheraner Handschrift (Bibliothek Malek, ms. 2487). Dissertation, Eberhard-Karls-Universität Tübingen, 170 pp. (TOBIAS-lib handle 10900/46247).
sources.note: 'Kurze Beschreibung der heutigen māzandarānischen Mundart' pp. 7-17 gives no general placement rule but scattered remarks: plural suffixes -(h)ā/-un 'nicht die Betonung auf sich ziehen' (p. 10-11); definite-object -e and indirect-object -ra unstressed (p. 11); substantivizing suffix -i stressed (p. 14); preterite prefixes ba-/da-/de-/ha-/hā- 'Das Präfix zieht hierbei den Wortakzent auf sich' (p. 15); infinitive ending -(j)en stressed (p. 17). Vowel length conditioned by stressed syllable (§2.1, p. 10).
